findings: The clean completion report is bound to revision f0fbd665dc683c38346d6c7de538955b526c4951 and the exact 5ffb35762ba9e9dd68eda56e34cfc8bda20fa70462d119ec645d48c1f0f22531 content digest. Workflow validation recomputed the BUG-118 fixed surface and, before this terminal record, reported only the expected missing reviews.jsonl condition for BUG-118; all 22 receipt pairs match their recorded SHA-256 hashes and all 17 required commands exit zero.

The ownership diagnosis matches both the live host and upstream source: libX11 1.7.5-1ubuntu0.3 resolves to libX11.so.6.4.0 with build ID 37a5d7bb..., while xorg/libX11 commit 1d11822601fd24a396b354fa616b04ed3df8b4ef adds the missing XFree(xim) after the internal close in _XimRegisterIMInstantiateCallback. The failed receipt preserves the 408-byte _XimOpenIM/_XimRegisterIMInstantiateCallback stack after engine initialization, and the helper proves glfwTerminate executes once.

The repository suppression set is guarded byte-for-byte in both process runners and the only new entry is leak:_XimRegisterIMInstantiateCallback; no loader, Mesa, ICD, pthread, module-wide X11/GLFW, or detect_leaks=0 escape was added. The symbolized direct diagnostic reports exactly one use totaling 408 bytes, and the platform runner requires the separate named 4096-byte allocation to exit 86 with a direct LeakSanitizer report before accepting the clean process. An independent execution of that exact CMake contract also passed.

LeakSanitizer function suppressions are stack-pattern scoped rather than allocation-object or byte-size scoped. The current evidence therefore supports the observed single 408-byte upstream row and preserves an unrelated synthetic engine leak, but the exception must remain interpreted narrowly and must not be generalized to hypothetical allocations made beneath the same XIM registration frame.

The selected-ICD qualification is truthful and bounded: the optional unqualified 53/54 receipt preserves the XIM row and two unsuppressed 256-byte unknown-module rows, the required NVIDIA-ICD exact shutdown selector passes 2/2, and the hash-bound full selected-ICD cohort passes 54/54. Hosted ci-vulkan likewise sets one explicit lavapipe VK_DRIVER_FILES value for its operational batch, so selecting one tested ICD is consistent with the production gate and does not convert driver-loader retention into a suppression.

Retirement synchronization is coherent: the done task has no unchecked actionable items and names Operational maturity plus implementation commit da893465; BUG-118 is closed in the bug index, linked from the retirement log and prior review, absent from active/session views, and its platform, Vulkan, and test READMEs state the current bounded contract. Fresh independent task-policy, task-schema, task-state-link, doc-link, docs-sync, layering, test-layout, root-hygiene, ARA, and source-documentation checks found no blocking defect.
